behavior_in_task_description.explanation: instruction.md specifies the exact file path (/app/submission/codec.py), the BITS/encode/decode interface and input/output formats, and every gate the grader checks: lossless, fixed length equal to the declared BITS, self-delimiting under appended padding, 64 KB size limit, determinism across two processes, and no filesystem side channels. It also gives the 108-bit target and the held-out grading set. The partial-credit formula is not spelled out, but the pass/fail target is explicit.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: verify.py, harness.py and gates.py test every stated requirement. They run encode twice and decode twice in separate processes as nobody, check alphabet, fixed length against BITS, losslessness on 10,000 held-out puzzles, padded decode, determinism, stray files across all world-writable roots, and source size. They also score BITS <= 108. The stdlib-only and no-network rules are enforced by the offline environment.

informative_test_structure.explanation: The grader is split into clear modules: gates.py (pure judging), harness.py (isolated phase execution), runner.py (child process) and verify.py (reward assembly). Docstrings and comments name each check, and the reward has a separate dimension per gate plus a readable report.txt.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The held-out puzzles are only in the verifier image, which runs in separate mode, and are chmod 0600 root while the codec runs as nobody. I confirmed train and held-out are disjoint. Only the single codec.py artifact is collected, with a 64 KB cap, so a catalogue lookup is impossible. Decode processes get codewords only, filesystem side channels are detected and purged, and there is no network.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The only structured output is the Python module interface. Its BITS constant and the encode/decode signatures and string formats are given explicitly and as normative in instruction.md.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: Both images use the pinned python:3.12.7-slim-bookworm, and the Node and Claude Code versions are pinned via ARGs. There are no pip dependencies; everything is stdlib. The apt packages are unpinned, which is acceptable.

typos.explanation: No typos found in paths, filenames or identifiers. The paths in the instruction, Dockerfiles, task.toml artifact, measure.py and verify.py candidates are consistent. The reference and tests copies of gates.py, harness.py and runner.py are identical.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: environment/Dockerfile copies only data, reference and submission. tests/ (including heldout.txt) goes only into the separate verifier image, and solution/ is not copied.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The grader needs only the Python standard library. No test-only dependencies are installed in the agent image, and the grading code and held-out data live only in the verifier image.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh installs a real algorithmic codec: a colex rank of the clue-position set combined with mixed-radix coding of each digit against the candidates its row, column and box still allow. It then runs measure.py. I checked that it round-trips all 49,151 train and held-out puzzles in 108 bits with padding appended.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: instruction.md explicitly names /app/submission/codec.py as the single deliverable, and it matches the task.toml artifact source and the grader's lookup path.
